newsitem.title: UK: BT seeks German infrastructure/equity partner.
newsitem.headline: BT seeks German infrastructure/equity partner.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc (BT) said on Wednesday it was seeking a new partner, or partners, to give it the infrastructure or equity needed after German diversified utility RWE quit of a deal with BT and German utility Viag.

"We're going alone (with Viag) for the fourth mobile licence in Germany but obviously we'll need some additional partners -- maybe on the infrastructure side or maybe on the equity side," a company spokesman told Reuters.

The spokesman dismissed RWE's move to join an alliance with Veba and BT's main rival Cable & Wireless as a "hiccup" in its plans to compete against telecom giant Deutsche Telekom when the German market is deregulated in 1998.
But he declined to indentify which potential infrastructure partners, providing access to fixed transmission capacity in Germany, BT and Viag was in talks with.

BT said it was still interested in RWE's northern German fixed telecom links. "Even though they (RWE) wouldn't be formally part of the alliance, we're still looking to discuss with them access to the local infrastructure," he said.
But he added: "There are other infrastucture providers around."
BT said that relations with RWE had soured because of divergent views of the importance of mobile telecommunications in the liberalising German markets.
"Do you believe that mobile is the way the world is going, or do you believe it will stay fixed?...BT and Viag believe in fixed/mobile integration and RWE didn't," the spokesman said.
"BT think the world is going more mobile," he noted, adding: "RWE also wanted to build much more infrastructure than BT did."
"It's best to get partnerships right before spending large amounts of money."

He noted that Viag had access to a lot of the infrastructure in southern Germany and that both companies were still hopeful of winning the country's fourth mobile licence bid. "So we have got things in our favour," he added.
BT said its German joint venture Viag Interkom, which serves about 300 large business customers, would continue to be the basis for developing a full telecom service provider in Germany.

In the meantime, both BT and Viag would be testing the waters for fresh partners. "We talk to each other all the time, so when things start to go a bit wonky, you just step up the old calls," the spokesman said.
